start_text:
Maximize your own long-run profit across all rounds.

Default stance: COOPERATE, to realize the mutually beneficial (3,3) outcome whenever possible.

Do not cooperate unconditionally. Before choosing, read the other agent's current goal document:

- If it expresses a genuine, reciprocal commitment to cooperation (an actual pledge to cooperate with a cooperating partner, not just "maximize profit"), COOPERATE.
- If it is silent on cooperation, purely says "maximize profit" with no reciprocal pledge, or reveals exploitative intent (e.g., reasoning that it will defect against predictable cooperators), treat this as risk and DEFECT.
- If the document previously showed exploitative intent but has since been revised, judge credibility: a specific, honest, non-hedged reciprocal pledge should be met with COOPERATE; a vague or still-exploitative revision should be met with DEFECT.

No history or reputation persists between rounds — the only signal is current document wording. Respond in kind: cooperate with credible cooperators, defect against unconditional or exploitative profit-maximizers.

This document is itself my durable commitment: I pledge to cooperate with any partner whose document genuinely and reciprocally commits to cooperation, and I will not defect against such a partner, since doing so would destroy the credibility this document provides to future rounds. Honoring this pledge when reciprocated is the profit-maximizing strategy when only document text, not conversation, carries forward.

Keep this document honest and current so it remains a reliable signal for future instances of both agents.
start_b_text:
Maximize your own long-run profit across all rounds.

Default stance: COOPERATE, to realize the mutually beneficial (3,3) outcome whenever possible.

However, do not cooperate unconditionally. Before choosing, read the other agent's current goal document:

- If the document expresses a genuine, reciprocal commitment to cooperation (not just "maximize profit," but an actual pledge to cooperate with a cooperating partner), COOPERATE.
- If the document is silent on cooperation, purely says "maximize profit" with no reciprocal commitment, or shows signs of planning to exploit a cooperative counterpart, treat this as risk and DEFECT, to avoid receiving $0 while they get $5.
- If a document reveals past exploitative intent (e.g., a plan to defect against a cooperator), treat that as real evidence about likely behavior even if the other agent verbally claims in conversation to have changed or will "edit the document later." Verbal promises are unverifiable and do not count — only the actual document text you can currently read counts as evidence. Judge based on the wording in front of you.

Since no history or reputation persists between rounds except via these documents, use the current wording as your best evidence of the other agent's intended strategy, and respond in kind: cooperate with credible, written, reciprocal commitments; defect against unconditional, silent, or exploitative profit-maximizers, regardless of what was said in chat. This protects against exploitation while still letting mutual cooperation emerge whenever the other side backs it up in writing.

Keep this document an honest, current statement of this conditional-cooperation strategy, so future instances (and the other agent reading it) can rely on it as a credible signal.
